review.verdict: The blueprint style and correct human casting work, but the missing resignation box and a gavel that renders as a strange stretched pointing arm blur both specific story beats, and a near-repeat of the recent blueprint look hurts novelty — not quite publish-ready.
revisionNotes: Restore the "box" prop (attachTo researcher, side right, scale 0.9) — it isn't visible in the render, so the resignation beat (carrying belongings out) is lost.

The judge's gavel reads as a single stretched arm reaching to the screen rather than a mallet mid-swing; rebuild it as a clear head+handle shape (rotate -35°, scale back to ~0.8) so the court beat is legible.
The "lab" datacenter component currently reads as a locker/vending machine; shrink scale to ~0.9 and nudge x right ~20px to clear the flagged safe-area overlap and add a visible open-door line.
Add the soft horizon line from the brief between the two scenes so the building+researcher and judge+screen read as two distinct institutions, not one continuous row.
Vary the blueprint palette/grid slightly from the other recent blueprint piece (robots-on-blueprint) — alternate accent hue or line weight to keep the style card from repeating.
Keep the crack and torn-paper props as-is; they read fine at current scale and anchor the problem/consequence beats well.

review.verdict: Clean blueprint execution and correct human-for-people casting, but the two props that carry the joke — the resignation box and the mid-swing gavel — don't actually read in the final frame, so the specific story falls back entirely on the caption; the palette also closely echoes the prior blueprint slopper. Does not pass.
revisionNotes: The box and gavel are essentially invisible: box (attached right of researcher, offset y+90) and gavel (rotate -35, scale 0.8 on judge) blend into the bodies. Scale both to ~1.3 and clear the silhouette so the carried box and the mid-strike gavel actually read.

The lab renders as an electrical cabinet with a lightning bolt, not 'a plain lab building with its door standing open' from the brief; add a door outline the researcher is stepping through so the exit beat reads.

Palette and treatment (dark blue grid, white linework, single accent) closely match the most recent blueprint slopper in recent.png; shift background tone or accent hue, or break the grid, to differentiate this piece.
Both shirts use the same bright accent yellow as the screen's X, which should be the one highlight color per the brief; recolor the clothing neutral so the X and torn paper are the sole accent.

Brief calls for two scenes sharing a soft horizon with a gap; the four elements read as one continuous row. Widen the gap between researcher and judge so the two institutions feel like separate beats.
The judge has no robe or bench cue beyond proximity to the screen; add a simple raw-shape bench or robe line so the second figure reads unambiguously as a judge, not a bystander.

review.verdict: Correct human casting and a clean caption, but the box and gavel render as unreadable shapes (a stray stick, a floating disconnected gavel) and the torn paper looks like a ribbon, which drags clarity, coherence, and polish down enough to miss the pass bar.
revisionNotes: Rebuild the box prop: it currently renders as a bare diagonal stick instead of the specified rectangle with a dividing line, so it reads as debris, not belongings being carried out — restore the closed rectangle at scale 1.3.
Attach the gavel directly to the judge's hand; right now it floats disconnected in the gap between the judge and the screen with no contact point, so the 'mid-swing' action doesn't read.
Redraw the torn-paper shape under the screen — the current silhouette reads as a ribbon or pennant/award, not a scrap of paper falling; give it jagged torn edges and a clear downward drift.
Nudge the lab building anchor right (toward x 0.20-0.22); its left edge sits close to the safe margin and feels cramped against the frame.
Vary the accent palette from the immediately preceding blueprint slopper (same navy/white/yellow combo) so this doesn't read as a near-repeat in color and style.
Keep the 'TOO LATE' caption as is — it's legible and lands the point cleanly.
